ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a vertical straight line, passing through points Q and T, and extending upward and downward; on the right side is a vertical straight line, passing through points R and S. Segment QR connects from Q downward to the right to R, and segment TS connects from T downward to the right to S. The figure marks QR ∥ TS, and the problem gives QT ∥ RS. ∠1 is located near point Q, and is the angle between the upward ray of the left vertical line and the slanted line QR; ∠4 is located near point T, and is the angle between the downward ray of the left vertical line and the slanted line TS. Reasoning: It is known that m∠1 = 131°. At point Q, ∠1 and the adjacent angle formed by the downward direction of the left vertical line and QR form a pair of linear angles, so that adjacent angle is 180° - 131° = 49°. Also because QR ∥ TS, and QT is the same vertical transversal, this corresponding angle of 49° is ∠4 at point T. Therefore m∠4 = 49°.

raw_record.question_text: In the figure, $QR \| TS$, $QT \| RS$, and $m\angle 1 = 131$. Find the measure of $\angle 4$.

method.method_draft: From the image, identify angle 1 at point Q as the angle between the upward extension of the left vertical line QT and the slanted segment QR, and identify angle 4 at point T as the angle between the downward extension of the same vertical line QT and the slanted segment TS. From the text, use QR || TS and m∠1 = 131°. Since angle 1 and the acute angle between downward QT and QR at Q form a linear pair, that acute angle is 180 - 131 = 49°. Because QR is parallel to TS and QT is the same transversal/vertical line through Q and T, the corresponding acute angle at T, namely ∠4, is also 49°.

method.method_draft: From the image, view the left vertical line through Q and T as having opposite rays: upward at Q for ∠1 and downward at T for ∠4. The slanted ray QR points down and right from Q, and the slanted ray TS points down and right from T. From the text, use QR || TS, so these two slanted rays have the same direction. If the angle from the upward vertical ray to the slanted direction is 131°, then the angle from the opposite vertical ray, the downward ray, to that same slanted direction is its supplement: 180 - 131 = 49°. Therefore ∠4 = 49°.
